data.title: Power Issue
data.description:
These power issues include:

  • The Phone does not turn on
  • The battery signal doesn’t show on the completely blacked-out phone. Therefore you can not determine the problem.
  • iPhone won’t stay charged. The charge drains rapidly after disconnecting from the adapter.
  • iPhone doesn’t charge. It is stuck on the battery percentage you left it to charge on.
  • Can’t use the iPhone without keeping it on a constant power supply (eg: Connected to a wall adapter or power bank etc,)

These frustrating problems are however the most common issues found on iPhone 6s. There are some widely renowned DIY (Do it yourself) fixes available on the internet which may help the issue on your device. Such as...

  • Force restarting your iPhone
  • Check Your Lightning cable and adapter and see if they are functioning properly.
  • Check if there is any debris on the iPhone 6s charging porthole.
  • Limit background processes by stopping the background app refresh.
  • Try charging while keeping your phone switched off.
  • Sometimes excessive battery drain can be happening due to a bug that can be resolved by a software update. So try updating your iOS to the latest version.

Wi-Fi gets disconnected on iPhone 6s.

Slow Wi-Fi speeds on metered/ non-metered connections on Wi-Fi.

High Latency/Ping on Wi-Fi connections

iPhone fails to connect to Wi-Fi

iPhone can’t discover your Wi-Fi connection.

These Wi-Fi issues found on iPhone 6s are pretty common issues found on other wireless supported devices too! And does not necessarily indicate that there is something specifically wrong with your iPhone 6s wireless hardware. There are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes available for your smartphone in this case.

Check your wireless router. Unplug it from the power source for 10 minutes and try again and see if the issues have been resolved.

Turn your Wi-Fi off for five minutes and try again.

Forget and reconnect your Wi-Fi connection.

Restore the default network connection

( Reset from here: Settings > General > Reset > Reset Network Connections > * Enter Passcode * > Confirm)

Update your iOS to the latest version available.

If none of the solutions mentioned above works to resolve your Wi-Fi issues on your iPhone 6s, you may need to get it checked by a professional technician.

data.description:

  • One near your proximity sensor, used for voice commands for Siri
  • The one in the back of your in the camera square. There is a tiny hole for the mic to pick up audio input while recording a video.

Now your microphone issue may be caused by any of the one or all 3 microphones not working. There are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes to try before you come to a decision.

Make sure if you use a protective cover for your phone. It doesn’t obstruct any speaker grills or mic holes.

Clear the phone to check and make sure there isn’t any debris in there.

Try recording your voice in a voice memo to make sure the mic works go to: Settings > Privacy > Microphone and make sure the app is listed there for it to use the microphone.

data.title: Network Problem
data.description:
These common issues however can be a network receptor hardware glitch of the iPhone 6s. To resolve these Apple recommends its iPhone 6s users some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes as a home remedy, such as:

  • Toggle Airplane Mode on and off to reset the previous network settings and cache.
  • Remove your sim card and reinstall it again. (requires a restart of the device)
  • Set up the internet for your phone if you’re facing internet issues through the network for the first time. To set up go to Settings > Mobile Data > Mobile Data Network

then:

  • Insert APN (Access Point Name) provided by your carrier 
  • Insert Username (provided by your carrier)
  • Insert Password (provided by your carrier)
  • Save the settings by pressing the left arrow at the top.
  • Make sure your Data connection is on after setting up the network before you access the internet.
  • Install carrier update for your iPhone (Check-in Settings > General > About)
  • Restart your iPhone
  • Soft reset your iPhone

If none of the solutions work for your iPhone, you might need your phone to get checked by a professional technician.   • Try Cleaning your lenses with a microfiber cloth. Be careful not to scratch it.
  • If your camera flash isn’t working, try turning on flash from the control center and see if it works.
  • You can also try resetting previous settings.
